summary: Lens-diverse task review of one diff, each finding adversarially verified by a skeptic panel

prior_findings.note: New test_role_passwords_are_the_ones_init_db_creates[dev|strict] uses _password_mismatches. It compares postgres SOLACE_APP_PASSWORD with POSTGRES_PASSWORD on every APP_SERVICES entry, and with the five legacy *_DB_PASSWORD aliases (user, diagnosis, therapy, memory, personality). Those five are the only *_DB_PASSWORD keys in either compose file. It also compares the password in the safety SAFETY_REPO_POSTGRES_DSN (user must be solace_app) and migrate DATABASE_URL against SOLACE_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD (user must be solace_migrator). It runs on the merged render of both profiles. Values are compared in-process and only service:NAME strings are reported. The strict and dev render values for app, migrator and superuser passwords are distinct (generated urlsafe24 in strict, different defaults in dev), so repointing any one entry to another source would be caught.

The postgres healthcheck is now pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -d solace && psql ... role check. The TCP probe cannot be answered by the entrypoint's socket-only init server. pg_isready sends no credentials, so it works under the hostssl-only hba, and no password appears in the command line. test_postgres_healthcheck_proves_tcp_before_the_role_check[dev|strict] pins the exact first command, the && order, and the psql role query. The real-infra healthcheck test still runs the new string.
